intro.heading: Company paperwork, off the board's desk
paragraphs: A [resident management company (RMC)](/who-we-work-with/rmc-and-rtm-directors/) is a company, usually owned by the leaseholders, that manages the building under the leases. As a director, you have duties under the Companies Act 2006. The company must file returns, keep registers and keep its records up to date.

Belgarum Property Management can act as your RMC's company secretary. A company secretary keeps the company's legal records and files its returns with Companies House. You keep your duties as a director. We do the paperwork that helps you meet them.

included.heading: What's included
items: Acting as the RMC's company secretary, appointed at Companies House
Filing the company's returns with Companies House, such as the yearly confirmation statement
Telling Companies House when directors join or leave
Keeping the share register up to date when flats are sold
A registered office service, so the company's official post comes to us

steps.title: Appointment
steps.text: The board appoints BPM as company secretary. We tell Companies House about the appointment.

steps.title: Registered office
steps.text: If the company uses our registered office service, its official address changes to ours. Post from Companies House and other official bodies then comes to us.

steps.title: Filings through the year
steps.text: We file the company's returns, including the confirmation statement. We tell Companies House about changes, such as a new director.

steps.title: Share register
steps.text: When a flat is sold, the RMC share usually passes to the buyer. We update the share register, so the company knows who its members are.

steps.title: The AGM

faqs.question: Does an RMC have to have a company secretary?
answer: No. Since 2008, private companies do not have to appoint one. But the work still has to be done: someone must file the returns and keep the registers. Many boards appoint a company secretary so it is done properly and on time.

faqs.question: What is a confirmation statement?
answer: A confirmation statement is a yearly filing that confirms the company's details at Companies House are correct, such as its directors, registered office and members. A company must file one at least once every 12 months. If it is not filed, the company can be struck off the register.

faqs.question: What are the legal duties of an RMC director?
answer: RMC directors have the same duties as directors of any company, under the Companies Act 2006. These include acting in the company's interests and making sure its filings are made. The directors keep these duties when they appoint a company secretary. For advice on your own duties, take independent legal advice.

faqs.question: Does an RMC have to hold an AGM?
answer: The Companies Act 2006 does not require private companies to hold an AGM. Many RMCs hold one because their articles of association require it, or because it is a good way to involve the members. Check your company's articles.

faqs.question: What happens to the RMC share when a flat is sold?
answer: In most RMCs, each leaseholder holds a share or membership. When the flat is sold, the share or membership passes to the buyer. The company secretary updates the share register so the company's records stay correct.
